corrections.text: The article says the Herald "found no independent replication of Mistral's FrontierCode, Terminal-Bench or cyber figures in the sources reviewed." The VentureBeat article it cites reports Artificial Analysis's own measurements: 25% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (against Mistral's 41%, from different evaluation contexts), 15% on FrontierCode 2.0 (against Mistral's 19.7%, with DeepSeek at 29% and GLM-5.3 at 22% in Artificial Analysis's results), a Cyber Index score of 51, and a Coding Agent Index score of 48. VentureBeat says the FrontierCode result does not support extending Mistral's first-place claim beyond the company's own comparison.

The "Conflicting Figures" section presents 49 billion and 52 billion active parameters as a disagreement between sources. The Hugging Face model card itself states 49 billion active parameters per token, or 52 billion including embeddings and output layers, and VentureBeat reports the same explanation. The two figures count different things rather than contradicting each other.
